an7.66:1.1: The sun is long associated with the number seven. It is conveyed by seven golden horses (Rig Veda 4.13.03, 5.45.9; Arthavaveda 13.2.23; Maitrāyaṇī Saṁhitā 4.12.4), and has seven rays (Rig Veda 8.72.16). The seven quarters each have their own sun (Rig Veda 9.114.3), thus seven suns are mentioned (Arthavaveda 13.3.10). Taittiriya Āraṇyaka 1.7.1.3 speaks of the seven Suryas, with Kaśyapa their head as the eighth, whose home Meru was reached by great rishis. If the numerological significance of the number seven is derived from the seven visible “planets”, one wonders what might happen if each of the caught fire.
an7.66:6.3: Anotatta (“unheated”) is mentioned as a mystical lake at [thag6.10:2.2](), while at [mil6.3.2:11.1]() it is said to be the source of the Ganges. The Buddha once ate his meal there ([pli-tv-kd1:19.2.1]()). | Moggallāna once procured some medicinal lotus for Sāriputta at the Mandākinī, there called “lotus pond”, with the help of a friendly mystical elephant ([pli-tv-kd6:20.1.8]()).
